Paper_Title: Are Autonomous Web Agents Good Testers? (PinATA / SeeAct-ATA)
Authors: J. Bergeron, F. Bordeleau, et al. [estimated]
Novelty: Empirically evaluates LLM-based Autonomous Test Agents (ATAs) that execute manual NL test cases and issue pass/fail verdicts; introduces PinATA (multi-agent decomposition) and SeeAct-ATA baseline; ~60% correct verdict, up to 94% specificity.
Advance_Over_Prior: Prior work stops at GENERATING test cases from business processes; this paper studies the EXECUTION+VERDICT step — the exact missing half of the IntelliTest thesis — and quantifies ATA reliability limits.
Relevance_To_Execution_Phase: VERY HIGH — directly about autonomous execution and oracle/verdict of functional UAT scenarios; primary anchor for the execution contribution.

Paper_Title: On the Soundness and Consistency of LLM Agents for Executing Test Cases Written in Natural Language
Novelty: Formal study of soundness (false failures from ambiguous NL) and consistency (nondeterministic re-runs) when LLM agents execute NL test cases.
Advance_Over_Prior: Prior work assumes generated cases are the deliverable; this exposes reliability/flakiness risks in the EXECUTION of NL tests — a threat-to-validity the new paper must address for its execution half.
Relevance_To_Execution_Phase: VERY HIGH — defines the reliability/flakiness challenge of NL-driven test execution agents; key related-work + threats-to-validity citation.

Novelty: Prototype AI-agent framework that, given a URL, autonomously explores a site, simulates real user interactions, detects bugs/usability issues, and produces human-readable reports.
Advance_Over_Prior: Adds autonomous EXPLORATION + bug/usability detection with human-like interaction, beyond static generation of business-process test cases.
Relevance_To_Execution_Phase: HIGH — autonomous web exploration and defect reporting is a form of the execution/UAT-agent capability.

Paper_Title: Autonomous Intelligent Agents for Natural-Language-Driven Web Execution with Integrated Security Assurance
Novelty: NL-driven web execution agents that generate Selenium scripts; raises script-generation success 55%->93%, 8x fewer navigation failures, 80% fewer timing races, 75% less test-creation time; integrates security assurance.
Advance_Over_Prior: Goes past generation into robust NL-to-executable-script EXECUTION with quantified reliability gains and security checks — directly relevant to production UAT execution.
Relevance_To_Execution_Phase: VERY HIGH — end-to-end NL-to-execution pipeline with concrete execution-reliability metrics.

Paper_Title: A Zero-Cost Self-Healing Approach Using DOM Accessibility Tree Extraction (Beyond LLM-based test automation)
Novelty: Replaces per-run LLM discovery with structured accessibility-tree extraction; self-heals only broken selectors (<1s, zero human intervention); scales to 300+ tests at zero ongoing API cost.
Advance_Over_Prior: Prior work does not touch execution maintenance; this tackles brittle-locator self-healing and DOM-abstraction for durable EXECUTION at scale/low cost.
Relevance_To_Execution_Phase: VERY HIGH — self-healing + DOM/accessibility-tree abstraction are core execution-phase mechanics.

Paper_Title: Practical Limits of Autonomous Test Repair: A Multi-Agent Case Study with LLM-Driven Discovery and Self-Correction
Novelty: Analyzes 300 autonomous execution reports / 636 test-case executions across 10 scenario families; 70% repair-convergence rate, mean 4.4 repair iterations.
Advance_Over_Prior: Provides empirical limits of autonomous self-repair during EXECUTION — grounds realistic expectations for the execution contribution.
Relevance_To_Execution_Phase: VERY HIGH — quantifies autonomous repair/self-correction during test execution.

Paper_Title: Framework and Benchmark for Code-Driven Agentic Testing in Web Development (CAT)
Novelty: Introduces Code-driven Agentic Testing: agent writes Playwright code to drive the browser, gathers feedback, autonomously explores web apps to find bugs; provides a benchmark for VLM bug-discovery.
Advance_Over_Prior: Introduces a paradigm and BENCHMARK for agentic end-to-end web execution/bug-finding — prior work lacked any execution benchmark.
Relevance_To_Execution_Phase: VERY HIGH — execution paradigm + benchmark; useful for evaluating the new execution half.

Paper_Title: HxAgent: Iterative Agent Planning for End-to-End Web Application Testing
Novelty: Iterative planning agent for E2E web testing; 97.4% Exact-Match on MiniWoB++, 83.8% EM / 91.8% Prefix-Match on 350 web tasks, beating WALT by 10-13%.
Advance_Over_Prior: Advances autonomous EXECUTION planning accuracy on web tasks well beyond static generation.
Relevance_To_Execution_Phase: HIGH — iterative execution planning for E2E web app testing.

Novelty: Five-agent LLM pipeline (Observer, Decider, Executor, Supervisor, Recorder) that maps app business logic to scenario-based GUI tests and executes them.
Advance_Over_Prior: Extends business-logic-aware testing into a MULTI-AGENT EXECUTION loop on mobile GUI, versus prior single-phase generation.
Relevance_To_Execution_Phase: HIGH — multi-agent architecture spanning perceive->decide->execute->verify; template for execution agents.

Paper_Title: Multi-Agent LLMs for End-to-End JUnit Test Generation with Accurate Oracles (CANDOR)
Novelty: Multi-agent LLM framework generating complete JUnit tests incl. oracles via a consensus panel discussion to curb hallucinated oracles.
Advance_Over_Prior: Improves ORACLE correctness through multi-agent consensus — advances the oracle quality problem beyond single-shot generation.
Relevance_To_Execution_Phase: MEDIUM — oracle-correctness techniques transfer to execution-verdict reliability.

Paper_Title: From Business Requirements to Test Assertions: Evaluating LLM-Generated Oracles on Real Bugs
Novelty: Evaluates LLM-generated oracles/assertions derived from business requirements against real bugs; finds oracles align more with requirements than with SUT and show high variance.
Advance_Over_Prior: Directly probes the requirements->oracle path used by the prior generation work, exposing its accuracy limits on real bugs.
Relevance_To_Execution_Phase: MEDIUM-HIGH — oracle reliability is central to autonomous verdicts in the execution phase.

Paper_Title: Agent-Based Test Assertion Generation via Diverse Perspective Aggregation
Novelty: Agent-based assertion generation that aggregates diverse LLM perspectives to produce stronger, more diverse assertions/oracles.
Advance_Over_Prior: Advances assertion/oracle strength via multi-perspective agents beyond single-model generation.
Relevance_To_Execution_Phase: MEDIUM — stronger oracles improve execution verdict fidelity.

Paper_Title: Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration for Unit Test Generation via Human-Testing-Inspired Workflows (TestAgent)
Novelty: LLM test generation emulating human testing practice through multi-agent collaboration.
Advance_Over_Prior: Multi-agent, human-workflow-inspired generation vs single-prompt business-process generation.

Paper_Title: DOM Tree Pruning Programming for Web Agent (Prune4Web)
Novelty: Shifts DOM handling from LLM reading of 10k-100k-token DOMs to LLM-generated executable Python scoring scripts that programmatically prune DOM elements.
Advance_Over_Prior: Novel DOM-ABSTRACTION technique that makes execution agents scalable on huge real-world pages.
Relevance_To_Execution_Phase: HIGH — DOM abstraction/scalability is a core execution-agent bottleneck.

Paper_Title: Manipulating LLM Web Agents with Indirect Prompt Injection via HTML Accessibility Tree
Novelty: Shows adversarial triggers embedded in HTML/accessibility tree can hijack LLM web agents into unintended actions.
Advance_Over_Prior: Introduces a SECURITY threat model for accessibility-tree-based execution agents absent from generation-only prior work.
Relevance_To_Execution_Phase: HIGH — security/threats-to-validity for DOM/accessibility-tree-driven execution agents.

Paper_Title: Acceptance Test Generation with Large Language Models (AutoUAT + Test Flow)
Novelty: Two-step LLM pipeline: user stories -> Gherkin scenarios (AutoUAT) -> executable Cypress scripts (Test Flow); industrially evaluated (95%/92% helpful).
Advance_Over_Prior: Closes the story->Gherkin->executable-script loop for UAT, moving beyond business-process case generation toward executable acceptance tests.
Relevance_To_Execution_Phase: HIGH — bridges generation to executable UAT scripts; adjacent to the execution contribution.

Paper_Title: The Potential of LLMs in Automating Software Testing
Novelty: Agent-oriented framework generating unit tests, visualizing call graphs, and automating test execution and reporting.
Advance_Over_Prior: Adds automated EXECUTION + reporting to generation, reducing human intervention across the loop.

Paper_Title: Evaluating LLMs for Multimodal GUI Test Generation in Android Applications
Novelty: Empirically evaluates multiple LLMs for multimodal (screenshot+DOM) GUI test generation; effectiveness varies by model.
Advance_Over_Prior: Provides recent multimodal GUI-testing evidence and model-comparison the new paper should cite.
Relevance_To_Execution_Phase: MEDIUM — multimodal GUI grounding informs execution-agent perception.

Paper_Title: KuiTest: Leveraging Knowledge in the Wild as GUI Testing Oracle for Mobile Apps
Novelty: Uses external in-the-wild knowledge as a GUI testing oracle where no executable spec exists (model-parametric oracle).
Advance_Over_Prior: Novel oracle strategy for GUI where prior work had no runtime oracle.
Relevance_To_Execution_Phase: MEDIUM-HIGH — oracle technique for execution-time verdicts on GUI.
